messages:
maria: quick heads-up from staging: observed duplicate partial chunks when an upstream does an early-flush and we fallback to resume — client sees repeated tokens and billing counts overlap.
alex: can you paste a minimal trace?
maria: trimmed repro: 
```
client -> edge (stream start)
edge -> upstream-A (streaming)
upstream-A: partial chunk, then TCP close (early-flush)
edge: forwards chunk to client, marks stream PREEMPTED
edge -> upstream-B: fallback/resume request
upstream-B: replays starting ~N tokens earlier
client: receives forwarded chunk + replayed chunk => duplicate content
```
sam: my guess: edge forwards in-flight bytes and also issues a token-based resume; two sources of truth.
maria: right. we currently set FORWARDED_UNCOMMITTED in the forward path but resume path ignores it.
jordan: naive fix: always prefer resume and drop forwarded bytes. but that will make clients miss immediate partial progress.
katie: other option: prefer forwarded-bytes if the time gap < threshold (client already saw it), else prefer resume for cost savings. per-tenant tunable.
alex: upstream compatibility problem: some upstreams accept resume offset headers (byte or token) and can trim; many only accept token checkpoints.
maria: proposal: edge emits a reservation id on early-flush and negotiates resume via headers: `X-Edge-Reservation: <id>` and `X-Edge-Resume-Mode: bytes|tokens`. Upstream that understands bytes mode will trim replays; upstream that doesn't will return 409/RESUME_MISMATCH.
sam: on 409 we need a deterministic policy: either drop the forwarded bytes (prefer-resume) or drop the resumed stream (prefer-forwarded). Should be tenant-configurable.
jordan: agree. Also need a short-lived reservation token (compact base64) to avoid leaked state.
katie: add metrics: duplicate_streams.count, bytes_trimmed.total, resume_mismatch.count, and a billing-impact gauge. dashboards and alert if duplicate_streams.rate > 0.1% of streams.
alex: implementation checklist:
- add reservation id in stream state (UUID/base64)
- emit `X-Edge-Reservation` + `X-Edge-Resume-Mode` on fallback request
- resume path consults FORWARDED flag and either signals upstream to trim or applies local trim if upstream supports it
- on upstream 409 -> consult tenant policy (prefer-forwarded | prefer-resume)
- record high-fidelity event for forensics (reservation id, tenant, policy outcome)
- expose staging flag `edge.resume_reservation` behind rollout gate
maria: ops playbook notes?
sam: include quick rollback: set policy to prefer-forwarded globally and disable header negotiation via `edge.resume_reservation=false`. Also add a sampling trace for 100% of resume events for first 24h after rollout.
jordan: security note: reservation token must be ephemeral and not replayable across long windows. rotate TTL to ~30s.
katie: UX: surface tenant-level knob in console and a per-route override. also add an alert runbook entry. i can help with dashboards.
alex: +1. please document backward compatibility: when upstream doesn't support headers, edge falls back to existing behavior unless policy dictates otherwise.
maria: i'll draft a short RFC and add a staging flag. will include header wire format and example logs. anyone object?
sam: +1, please include tests for partial-bytes vs token resume, and a fuzz test for boundary off-by-one token duplicates.
jordan: +1. add a metric for how often we hit 409 to monitor adoption.
katie: +1. i'll sketch dashboard layout.
alex: +1. infra-bot: can you gate a canary for the new flag?
infra-bot: gating created: rollout group alpha-ops; flag `edge.resume_reservation` default off; can enable for orgs: ops-test.
maria: thanks all 44d i'll convert to RFC and ping reviewers.
